## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring (`K` stops a process: SIGTERM, up to 5 s, then a confirmed SIGKILL on Linux and macOS, at once on Windows; DevDesk itself, its direct parent, PID 1 and Windows PIDs 0 and 4 are refused; the identity is checked at each signal, DEVDESK-711) + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when no configured helper is `store` (plaintext) or `cache` (memory with a timeout), by name, path or shell command: `approve` reaches every helper. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one. Every host store operation (the probe, `Save`, `Load`,
`Delete`) is bounded to 3 s: a store that does not answer, such as a locked
Secret Service waiting on an unlock prompt over SSH, is skipped like an absent
one, `Detail` says so, and it is not asked again while that call is stuck
(`internal/credentials/hoststore_bound.go`, DEVDESK-745).

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view. It takes the `Selection` and moves nothing when it does not
persist (memory), and removes a secret from the YAML only once it reads back
from the store; otherwise it stays and the note says so (DEVDESK-745).

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.
The renderers (helm, kustomize) run with the network cut (DEVDESK-767, D180):
`containerRun.Offline` (`--network none`, no proxy) from an image, `offlineEnviron` from a binary,
except kustomize with `scan.tools.kustomize.allow_remote_bases: true`; a refused remote base is the
K8S-RENDER finding `Overlay does not build: remote base blocked` (`remoteBlocked`).

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708, DEVDESK-711).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill(pid, want, sig)` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam, which also holds `identity` and `probe` (`Probe` reads the state, it
sends no signal). `selfPID`, `parentPID`, `goos` and `now` are seams too. A test substitutes them
(`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`); in `internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps`
on the model, so `ports.Kill`, `ports.Terminate` and `ports.Probe` are never reached.
`IdentityForTest` and `DeferredIdentityForTest` panic outside a test binary.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`, `TestTerminateEndsARealChildProcess` in
`stop_real_test.go`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

832	### Writing a Resolution, Steps and Repro for a new finding (adopted)
833	
834	The parser that builds a finding in `internal/scan` writes, beside its constructor, a `Resolution`
835	(one paragraph) and, when the fix has distinct actions, `Steps`: imperative English US sentences, one
836	action each, alternatives as separate steps, no key name (the same fix is read in the detail, in
837	`scan_result` and in the README, and a key is true in only one of them), and the tool or the
838	Kubernetes version named when it decides the answer. A `Repro` is built only through `localRepro`
839	(or a wrapper of it such as `renderRepro`), never assembled by hand, so the `PlainWords` refusal, the
840	"no line from a container" rule and the "never copy `scan.tools.*.args`" rule always apply. Text written
841	by a third party (Trivy, plumber) is never restructured: it stays in `Resolution` as the scanner wrote
842	it.
843	
844	The reviewer checks this like the other rules; the techwriter is called in only to rewrite a text in
845	depth. Two tests in `internal/scan` hold what a machine can hold:
846	
847	- `steps_guard_test.go` reads every list a `*Steps` function of `steps.go` returns (inputs for each
848	  branch, in `stepSamples`; `TestEveryStepsFunctionHasASample` finds the functions by parsing
849	  `steps.go`, so a new one that has no sample fails) and fails on a key name (a `ctrl+`, `alt+`,
850	  `shift+` or `cmd+` chord, `esc`, `ctrl`, a usual key name or a capital letter between angle brackets
851	  (`<Enter>`, `<Y>`; a placeholder such as `<chart>` is fine), `F1` to `F12`, "enter key" and its kin,
852	  "hit the key", the words press, keystroke, keybinding, shortcut), an empty or multi-line step, a step
853	  that does not start with a capital letter or end with a period, and a duplicate. The one exception is
854	  inherited, and must not serve as a model: the exact two-step alternative of a load restrictor failure
855	  ("Reference a directory that has its own kustomization.yaml, or" then "move the file below ..."), whose
856	  text is frozen by several tests and the scan cache. Any other step ending in ", or" is refused; write
857	  alternatives as separate sentences that each end with a period. Not checked, for lack of a reliable check: that the first word is an imperative verb,
858	  that a step holds one action, that the English is US; a bare "enter" or "tab" is not flagged (also a verb or a noun).
859	- `provenance_guard_test.go` parses the non-test sources of `internal/scan` and fails when a `Repro` of a
860	  `Finding` is set from anything but `localRepro` or a wrapper the guard finds by itself (a function whose
861	  every return is a call to a producer), and when a `Steps` is set from anything but a `*Steps` function; a second test fails on any `*Steps`
862	  function defined outside `steps.go` (the only file `stepSamples` covers), so a free-text producer cannot
863	  hide behind the name.
864	  A site is `Repro: x`, `f.Repro = x` or `f.Repro, f.RanFrom = a, b`; `x` must be a producer call, a name only a
865	  producer defined in the function, or a parameter that every caller in the package feeds that way. Each
866	  rule has a synthetic source that breaks it and must be flagged, so the detector can fail. Limits: it matches
867	  names, not types (any struct with a `Repro` or `Steps` field is held to it); an alias, a function value, a
868	  pointer to the field, reflection and a `Finding` built by another package are out of its sight; flow inside a
869	  function is ignored (a name also assigned from something else is refused); functions are keyed by name.

I'm weighing whether to refuse absolute paths in the whitelist, since the user's criterion is a safe local path without a scheme, host, or `@`, and absolute paths are local, but the rest of that thought about symlinks escaping the directory is cut off here.

I'm weighing whether a path outside the repository should be refused even though it's local, since following a directory there could still reach files I can't vouch for. My leaning is to refuse absolute paths outright, as kustomize itself does. That refusal needs its own message, distinct from the remote-base headline, so the user knows the reference leaves the repository.

I'm settling on the message for blocked references: it should name the overlay file and the specific entry, like `resources[0]`, and say why it was refused, and I'll keep control characters out of it by quoting with `%q`. Since kustomize never ran in that case, the reproduction stays empty, and I'd leave it empty for the undecidable case too, since a copied `kustomize build` might still fetch something.

I'm now sorting out how the overlay's directory gets resolved: native runs only when the tool isn't a container, so container argv stays the same. The overlay path joins the target directory, and the boundary check has to compare the scope root and target with symlinks resolved on both sides.

I'm checking whether the gate should also cover missing leaf files, like a configMap's secret file: a path that doesn't exist can't fetch anything, so kustomize can report the missing file itself rather than the gate refusing it.

I'm checking whether a bare relative resource like `foo` can reach the network: kustomize would try to load it as a file, then as a repo URL with no host, then as a directory, and all of those fail locally. The lexical rule already rejects colons, `@`, and a leading `github.com` segment, and the parser only treats a reference as remote when one of those is present, so a plain local name can't trigger a fetch.

I'm checking whether a backslash on Windows should also be refused, since kustomize may treat it as a separator, and I'm keeping that question open.

I'm deciding that missing files can't fetch anything, so a missing leaf file should be left for kustomize to report rather than refused by the gate, but I'm still weighing whether a missing path in resources needs the same treatment.

I'm settling on a missing path as something to hand to kustomize, since a local name that doesn't exist can't fetch anything and it will report the error itself. A path that exists but can't be read, whether from permissions, size, not being a regular file, or a symlink leading outside, gets refused instead. I'm treating that missing-path case as a working assumption rather than a settled rule.

I'm working out that a directory reached through generators or transformers could hold plugin configs, since kustomize accumulates whatever a referenced kustomization contains, so I'll need to follow those directories too.

I'm settling the plugin-config walk: a directory reached through transformers or generators has its resource files parsed as plugin configs, so the walk needs a mode that tracks that, while normal resources are treated as plain objects. I'm also checking whether a resource document can trigger a fetch on its own, and it can't with default flags, since KRM function annotations only matter in generators and transformers. The anchors and aliases are still pending.

I'm checking how kustomize's YAML parser handles duplicate keys, since a mismatch with my own parser could hide content from the gate.

I'm checking how kustomize unmarshals the kustomization file, whether it uses a strict mode that would reject unknown fields, since a mismatch with my parser could let ambiguous content through.

I'm weighing the boundary for native kustomize: it stays at the target, so an overlay that references `../../base` outside a scanned subfolder would get refused, which breaks the purely local overlay case. One option is to set the boundary to the git toplevel instead.

I'm going with option A: the boundary becomes the git toplevel via resolveRenderScope, even for native kustomize run offline, since the user's "dépôt" means the repo. I'd compute that boundary separately as a gate root so the scope used by native helm stays untouched, which avoids breaking any test that expects git not to be queried when no container runs.

I'm settling the boundary question for lexical `..` paths: I'd treat them like symlinks, bounded by the repo (git toplevel, or the scanned directory when there's no git), so anything escaping gets refused. Whether to ask the user about this is still open; I'll proceed with that default and note the missing-leaf case as a hypothesis rather than a blocker.

I'm checking how plugin mode should treat the sub-kustomization's resource files, which are plugin configs there, and I'm planning a walk function that takes a plugin-mode flag. Each resource document would need apiVersion exactly "builtin" and a kind from the builtin list, matched exactly.

I'm checking whether the plugin-config match is case-insensitive too, since the Config gets unmarshalled through sigs.k8s.io/yaml. I'll treat plugin fields with EqualFold like the rest, and refuse any non-builtin plugin outright, since that stays closed.

I'm treating inline generator and transformer entries as plugin configs: if an entry parses as a mapping, I check each document in it; if it's a plain path string, it gets classified as a path instead.

I'm deciding how to classify patchesStrategicMerge entries: if the entry is an existing local file, kustomize treats it as a path, and otherwise as inline patch content. I'm checking the edge case where a string like "a: b" could also be a real filename, which still resolves to a local file rather than a remote one. The URL-like entries starting with http are the ones I still need to handle.

I'm checking the remaining edge cases in patch and generator entries: a `http:`-prefixed path that happens to exist locally gets read as a file and then fetched remotely, but the colon rule refuses it anyway. I'll also check `patches[].path` alone, since setting both `path` and `patch` is an error in kustomize, and cover `replacements[].path`, `openapi.path`, and the `key=path` form in configMapGenerator files.

I'm checking the remaining URL-like forms: a `//host/path` string has no scheme, so it isn't treated as remote, and on Linux it's an absolute path that gets refused anyway. That means the colon-and-`@` lexical rule covers New and Load as well.

Now I'm checking the remaining edge cases in the generator and patch entries for remote fetches. The specific things to verify are `replacements[].path`, `openapi.path`, and the `key=path` form in configMapGenerator files, and whether a `//host/path` string slips past the colon rule. It doesn't: it has no scheme, and on Linux it's an absolute path that gets refused anyway. Existing tests that use remote resources with a fake runner will now hit the gate first, so they need review.

I'm going over the test updates the kustomize gate will need, then checking the docs that still describe allow_remote_bases, and finally deciding whether the backlog entry should be a new number or an update to D180.

I'm laying out the design steps now: a lexical rule in a new kustomize gate file, with a table of accepted and refused references to test it.

I'm listing the refused reference forms for the lexical rule: localhost and IPv6 URLs, case variants, scp-style git addresses, ssh and file schemes, git:: prefixes, GitHub shorthands with subpaths and query strings, user@host forms, absolute and UNC and drive-letter paths, empty strings, and control characters. Those will go in the table alongside the accepted local forms. I'm keeping this step independent of the YAML hygiene reader, so the two can be built in parallel.

I'm laying out the third step: a walker in the kustomize gate, `vetOverlay`, that goes through each field of the kustomization schema, follows resource, base and component directories, treats generators, transformers and validators as plugin configs, and checks symlinks, `..` escapes, size and cycle limits. I'll cover it with one test per field, plus cases for a local base holding a reference, a transformer file, an inline transformer, an unknown key, an unknown plugin, a function annotation, and symlinks or `..` paths that leave the repo.

I'm laying out the rest of the plan: the walker's coverage of depth and count caps, unreadable files, two kustomization files in one directory, missing leaf paths passing through, and a cycle between bases terminating, which kustomize itself reports. Next is wiring the gate into the render path with the boundary computed separately from the scope, emitting an unchecked finding with its title, steps and empty repro. The tests will cover native offline remote references not reaching the runner, the unjudgeable title, and pure local overlays keeping the exact command and offline environment.

I'm setting up the real-kustomize loopback acceptance test with a counting server, gated on kustomize being at least 5.8.3. I'll cover each loopback variant (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1], 127.0.0.2, and a `*.localhost` name), skipping any the environment can't support.

I'm going through the remaining loopback cases for the real-kustomize test: git won't fetch over the blocked protocol, but curl may still route localhost through a proxy, so I'm checking that the counting server sees zero requests with the gate on and at least one with it off. I'll also update the existing remote-bases test so its four remote cases assert the blocked title.

Now I'm turning to the last pieces: the remote-bases test should move to a direct kustomize run with the offline environment so the defense-in-depth marker is still measured. Then I'll handle the text and docs changes, including the Resolution wording and the D180 amendment, which may belong to the wiring step.

I'm setting the gate's risks aside for a moment: the parser-difference concern is handled by refusing anchors, tags, merge keys, duplicate and non-ASCII keys, and multi-document files, and the remaining scalar differences only matter where kustomize would error anyway. The other risk is version drift, since the field list was measured on kustomize 5.8.3, so I'm checking how closed top-level keys would refuse an unknown field from a newer release.

I'm drafting the remaining risk notes: version drift on kustomize, since the field list was measured on 5.8.3 and a recorded fixture comparison is the practical check, and a possible race between the gate's check and kustomize's later read of the files.

I'm checking the leftover risks: a concurrent checkout could change files between the gate's check and kustomize's read, which I'll accept and document. I also need to note the user-passed flags like `--enable-helm` and `--helm-command`, which the gate doesn't cover, and whether helm rendering stays offline.

I'm noting the remaining risks: the gate could run into unmeasured cases like Windows paths or helm options passed by the user. I'm also checking behavior changes such as refusing overlays that reach outside the boundary, and the performance cost of re-reading kustomization files per overlay, which I could memoize per stage. The remoteBlocked marker path should only matter if the gate passes but kustomize still fetches, which I don't expect, and since nothing changes in the schema or config, reverting is enough and D180 just needs amending.

I'm drafting the message for the blocked remote base, with a title constant and keeping the File field on the overlay's kustomization since that is the leaf being validated. I also need to note that the existing remote-bases test measures the markers under the old flow, and that the deprecated helm inflation generator fields such as chartRepoUrl need to be refused when non-empty.

I'm checking the remaining Helm-related kustomize fields for remote reach: `extraArgs` could smuggle in a `--repo` URL, and `helmCharts[].repo` needs refusing when non-empty. Local paths like `configHome` and `chartHome` stay path-checked, since a local chart rendered offline doesn't touch the repositories config.

Next I'm checking the remaining kustomize fields that could carry a remote reference, like `openapi.path`, `crds`, and `configurations`, along with `validators` and `sortOptions`.

## DEVDESK-771 : plan pour fermer la loopback du kustomize natif (liste blanche fermée)

**Questions bloquantes**
- **Q1. Où s'arrête le dépôt pour un chemin en `..` ?** Ta décision couvre un lien symbolique qui sort du dépôt, pas un chemin `..` qui en sort. Or en natif, `v.scope` vaut aujourd'hui la cible scannée : git n'est appelé que pour un conteneur (`kubeconform.go:146`).
  - (a) La limite est le dépôt git. On la calcule à part, dans `v.gateRoot`, avec `resolveRenderScope`, sans toucher `v.scope`. Sans git, la limite est la cible scannée. Tout ce qui sort de la limite est refusé, même règle que les liens symboliques. **Recommandé.** Conséquence : scanner un sous-dossier hors git dont un overlay référence `../base` donnerait désormais un refus.
  - (b) Un `..` peut aller n'importe où sur la machine (lu et contrôlé là où il mène). Seuls les liens symboliques sont bornés.

**1. Points d'accroche**
- Le rendu natif est lancé dans `renderKustomizations` (`internal/scan/kubeconform_render.go:379-421`). La garde s'insère juste après `scope = scope.cut()` et avant `kustomizeArgs`, si `scope.offline && tool.Source != ToolSourceContainer`. En cas de refus : on ajoute le finding, on fait `continue`, et `runner.Run` n'est jamais appelé.
- Aujourd'hui, `remoteBlocked` (`render_network.go:66`) lit stderr, puis les lignes 403-409 remplacent Title, Resolution et Repro. Ce remplacement passe dans un helper `markRemoteBlocked(*Finding)`, partagé entre ce chemin et la garde. `remoteBlocked` et `offlineEnviron` restent en seconde barrière.
- Nouveau fichier `internal/scan/kustomize_gate.go` :
  - `func localRef(ref string) (bool, string)` ;
  - `func readGateYAML(p string, b *gateBudget, multiDoc bool) ([]*yaml.Node, error)` ;
  - `func vetOverlay(ctx context.Context, root, overlay string, lim gateLimits) gateVerdict`, avec `gateVerdict{Kind gateOK|gateRemote|gateUnchecked; File, Field, Ref, Reason string}`.
- `steps.go` : nouvelle fonction `uncheckedOverlaySteps(target, reason string) []string`, plus son échantillon dans `stepSamples`.
- Nouvelles constantes : `uncheckedOverlayHeadline` (proposé : `Overlay not built: its references could not be checked`) et `uncheckedOverlayResolution`.

**2. Champs relevés dans kustomize 5.8.3**
Le binaire installé est v5.8.3 (api et kyaml v0.21.3) ; source lue dans `~/go/pkg/mod/sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/api@v0.21.3`.

Deux portes d'entrée réseau, et seulement deux :
- `FileLoader.Load` (HTTP GET si `url.Parse` donne le schéma http ou https) ;
- `FileLoader.New`, via `git.NewRepoSpecFromURL` : un clone git s'il y a un schéma `ssh://`, `https://`, `http://` ou `file://`, un préfixe `git::`, un `user@`, **ou un chemin qui commence par `github.com/` ou `github.com:` (casse ignorée), même sans schéma**.

| Champ | Ce que kustomize en fait |
|---|---|
| `resources`, `bases` | Essayé comme fichier (`Load`), puis comme répertoire ou dépôt git (`New`) |
| `components` | `New` |
| `crds`, `configurations` | `Load` |
| `openapi.path` | `Load` |
| `patches[].path`, `patchesJson6902[].path` | `Load` |
| `patchesStrategicMerge[]` | Chemin si le fichier existe, sinon patch inline |
| `replacements[].path` | `Load` |
| `configMapGenerator` et `secretGenerator` : `files[]` (forme `clé=chemin`), `envs[]`, `env` | `Load` |
| `helmGlobals.chartHome` / `configHome` | Chemins |
| `helmCharts[]` : `repo` / `valuesFile`, `additionalValuesFiles`, `chartHome` | URL / chemins |
| `helmChartInflationGenerator[]` (ancien format) : `chartRepoUrl`, `helmBin`, `extraArgs` / `chartHome`, `helmHome`, `values` | Valeurs libres / chemins |
| `generators`, `transformers`, `validators` | Config de plugin inline, ou chemin (fichier ou répertoire) |

Les autres champs ne portent aucune référence : apiVersion, kind, metadata, namePrefix, nameSuffix, namespace, commonLabels, labels, commonAnnotations, images, imageTags, replicas, vars, sortOptions, generatorOptions, buildMetadata.

Plugins intégrés (`apiVersion: builtin`) et leurs champs chemin :
- ConfigMapGenerator et SecretGenerator : `files`, `envs`, `env` ;
- PatchTransformer et PatchJson6902Transformer : `path` ;
- PatchStrategicMergeTransformer : `paths[]` ;
- ReplacementTransformer : `replacements[].path` ;
- ValueAddTransformer : `targetFilePath` ;
- HelmChartInflationGenerator : mêmes règles que `helmCharts`.

**Règle de liste blanche retenue.** Un chemin est accepté s'il remplit toutes ces conditions :
- non vide ;
- aucun `:`, ce qui couvre schéma, `host:`, `git::` et lettre de lecteur Windows. C'est plus strict que « pas de `host:` » ; un nom de fichier contenant `:` sera refusé ;
- aucun `@`, aucun `?`, aucun caractère de contrôle ;
- pas absolu, et ne commence ni par `/` ni par `\` (le chemin UNC Windows ouvrirait une connexion SMB) ;
- premier segment différent de `github.com` (casse ignorée). Sans ce point, ta règle laisserait passer `github.com/o/r` ; `./github.com/o/r` reste accepté ;
- reste dans la limite de Q1, une fois le chemin nettoyé puis les liens symboliques résolus avec `EvalSymlinks`.

Les noms avec un point (`v1.2/base`) sont acceptés. J'ai vérifié en lisant `IsRemoteFile` et `NewRepoSpecFromURL` que cette règle exclut les deux portes réseau de la version 5.8.3.

Valeurs qui ne sont pas des chemins :
- `patches[].patch`, et une entrée `patchesStrategicMerge` dont le contenu est un mapping YAML : ce sont des données, acceptées ;
- `helmCharts.repo`, `chartRepoUrl`, `helmBin`, `extraArgs` non vides : refusés comme base distante (`extraArgs` peut contenir `--repo`) ;
- une entrée de `generators`, `transformers` ou `validators` qui se lit comme un mapping : c'est une config de plugin, contrôlée comme un fichier de plugin ;
- un répertoire cité dans `generators`, `transformers` ou `validators` : on le suit en mode plugin, où ses fichiers `resources` sont lus comme des configs de plugin.

Dans une config de plugin, est refusé comme « non jugeable » tout document dont l'`apiVersion` n'est pas exactement `builtin`, dont le `kind` est inconnu, ou qui porte l'annotation `config.kubernetes.io/function` ou `config.k8s.io/function`.

**Écart entre analyseurs YAML.** kustomize lit avec `YAMLToJSON` puis le décodeur JSON, qui compare les clés en ignorant la casse, y compris le repli Unicode (`ſ` vaut `s`, `K` vaut `k`). La garde fait les mêmes correspondances avec `strings.EqualFold`, et elle échoue fermé (refus) dans tous ces cas :
- ancre ou alias, clé de fusion `<<`, tag explicite (`!!binary` cacherait une URL encodée en base64), clé qui n'est pas un scalaire ;
- clé en double (casse ignorée), clé non ASCII ;
- plusieurs documents dans une kustomization, deux fichiers kustomization dans un même répertoire ;
- clé de premier niveau inconnue ;
- valeur de référence qui n'est pas une chaîne.

Un fichier ou un répertoire de kustomization qui manque, n'est pas un fichier régulier ou est trop gros donne un refus « non jugeable ».

*Hypothèse :* une feuille absente (ex. `files: [missing.txt]`) passe et kustomize signale lui-même l'erreur. Comme elle est déjà validée lexicalement, aucun accès réseau n'est possible.

**3. Plafonds proposés** (`defaultGateLimits`, valeurs non mesurées)
- Profondeur : 16.
- Kustomizations visitées par overlay : 256, avec un mémo des répertoires déjà vus pour qu'un cycle se termine sans être signalé.
- Taille d'un fichier analysé : 4 MiB, comme `k8s.maxManifestSize`.
- Total lu par overlay : 32 MiB.
- `ctx.Err()` est vérifié à chaque fichier.

Tout dépassement donne un refus « non jugeable » qui nomme le plafond atteint.

**4. Plan TDD** (pour chaque étape, les tests s'écrivent d'abord)

1. **`localRef`.** Test table, côté accepté : `base`, `../base`, `./x.yaml`, `v1.2/base`, `./github.com/o/r`, `a b/c.yaml`. Côté refusé, chacun avec sa raison : http et https vers 127.0.0.1, localhost, `[::1]`, 127.0.0.2 ; `HTTP://` en majuscules ; `git@h:o/r` ; `ssh://` ; `file://` ; `git::https://` ; `github.com/o/r` ; `GitHub.com/o/r//s?ref=v1` ; `u@h/x` ; `/abs` ; `\\srv\s` ; `C:\x` ; `x?ref=1` ; chaîne vide ; caractère de contrôle. Étape parallélisable avec la 2.
2. **`readGateYAML`.** Un test par refus de la section 2 : ancre, alias, `<<`, `!!binary`, double `Resources`/`resources`, `reſources`, multi-documents, clé non scalaire, fichier de plus de 4 MiB, fichier non régulier, permission 000 (sauté si on tourne en root).
3. **`vetOverlay`.** Dépend des étapes 1 et 2.
   - Test table : une URL de loopback dans **chaque** champ du tableau, et dans chaque champ de chaque plugin, attend `gateRemote` avec `Field` et `File` exacts.
   - Une base locale dont le kustomization porte l'URL.
   - Un transformer en fichier, un transformer inline, un répertoire suivi en mode plugin.
   - Les refus : plugin inconnu, annotation de fonction, clé inconnue, lien symbolique de base ou de kustomization qui sort du dépôt, `..` hors limite, plafonds de profondeur, de nombre et d'octets, deux fichiers kustomization.
   - Les acceptations : un cycle a→b→a donne OK ; un overlay entièrement local qui utilise tous les champs donne OK.
4. **Branchement dans `renderKustomizations`.** Dépend de l'étape 3. Tests avec `useRunner` :
   - natif, hors ligne, URL : kustomize n'est **pas** appelé ; ID K8S-RENDER, HIGH, Title `remoteBlockedHeadline`, Repro vide, Message qui nomme le fichier, le champ et la référence (en `%q`) ;
   - cas non jugeable : le Title et les Steps dédiés ;
   - overlay local : commande, arguments et environnement identiques à avant ;
   - `AllowRemoteBases` à vrai : garde non appelée, `Env == nil` ;
   - source conteneur avec une URL : garde non appelée, argv identique à la référence actuelle.

   Il faudra aussi mettre à jour `stepSamples` et vérifier que `provenance_guard` reste vert.
5. **Tests d'acceptation avec un vrai kustomize ≥ 5.8.3** (sautés sinon), dans `render_network_test.go`. Dépend de l'étape 4.
   - Un `httptest` qui compte les requêtes, pour chaque variante : 127.0.0.1 ; `localhost` ; `[::1]` (sauté s'il n'y a pas d'IPv6) ; 127.0.0.2 (sauté si le listen échoue, cas de macOS) ; un nom `x.localhost` (témoin sauté s'il ne se résout pas).
   - Pour chaque variante : 0 requête, et un témoin avec `allow_remote_bases: true` qui doit donner au moins 1 requête.
   - `TestARealKustomizeIsRefusedItsRemoteBases` attend aujourd'hui les marqueurs stderr. Avec la garde, kustomize n'est plus lancé et ce test va échouer. On le scinde :
     - un test de bout en bout : titre « blocked » et kustomize non lancé ;
     - un test qui lance kustomize directement avec `offlineEnviron`, pour continuer à mesurer la seconde barrière.
   - Les autres tests natifs d'`internal/scan` qui injectent un stderr de blocage sur un overlay portant une URL sont à adapter de la même manière.
6. **Textes et documentation.** Parallélisable avec l'étape 5 une fois la 4 faite.
   - Textes qui doivent dire qu'`allow_remote_bases` inclut les services de cette machine : `remoteBlockedResolution`, l'étape « blocked » de `renderSteps`, `hintOn` dans `scan_fields.go` et son test `kustomize_remote_bases_test.go`, le commentaire de `KustomizeConfig`.
   - Dans `docs/architecture/scanning.md`, la limite (1) est remplacée par la garde : champs, règle, plafonds, limites.
   - Dans D180 : le point 2 est amendé (le filtre par URL rejeté reste rejeté ; ici c'est une liste blanche de chemins), le point 5 aussi, et un point DEVDESK-771 est ajouté.
   - À mettre à jour aussi : `network.md`, `configuration.md`, `docs-site/docs/{reference/configuration,explanation/scanning}.md`, la ligne de `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

**5. Risques et limites à documenter**
- La liste est relevée sur kustomize 5.8.3. Une version plus récente qui ajoute un champ de premier niveau voit ses overlays refusés (liste fermée). Une nouvelle façon d'aller sur le réseau à l'intérieur d'un champ déjà connu ne serait vue que par `offlineEnviron`, qui laisse passer la loopback. Je recommande une liste de champs enregistrée en `testdata` avec un test de concordance, à refaire à chaque montée de version.
- Le dépôt peut changer entre la garde et le lancement de kustomize (TOCTOU). Le dépôt est supposé immobile pendant le scan.
- Arguments ajoutés par l'utilisateur :
  - `--enable-alpha-plugins`, `--enable-exec` : ils ne servent plus à rien, puisque tout plugin non intégré est refusé ;
  - `--enable-helm` avec un chart local : `helm template` est lancé avec l'environnement coupé ; les dépendances du chart ne sont pas récupérées, ce que je n'ai pas mesuré ;
  - `--load-restrictor` : non concerné.
- Changements de comportement :
  - noms de fichier contenant `:`, `@` ou `?` refusés ;
  - champ de premier niveau inconnu refusé ;
  - références hors de la limite refusées (Q1) ;
  - le cache sert l'ancien résultat jusqu'au prochain scan ;
  - Windows n'a pas été mesuré.
- Le champ `File` du finding reste le kustomization de l'overlay (*Hypothèse*) ; le fichier qui porte la référence est nommé dans le Message.
- Coût : tous les kustomizations sont relus pour chaque overlay. Un mémo par étape de scan est possible.
- Rien d'irréversible : pas de schéma ni de clé nouvelle, un revert suffit. Pas besoin d'ADR, l'amendement de D180 suffit.

**6. Questions bloquantes :** Q1 seulement (en tête). Le titre « non jugeable » est une proposition que l'UX peut changer ; ce n'est pas bloquant.

- ConfigMapGenerator et SecretGenerator : `files`, `envs`, `env` ;
- PatchTransformer et PatchJson6902Transformer : `path` ;
- PatchStrategicMergeTransformer : `paths[]` ;
- ReplacementTransformer : `replacements[].path` ;
- ValueAddTransformer : `targetFilePath` ;
- HelmChartInflationGenerator : mêmes règles que `helmCharts`.

**Règle de liste blanche retenue.** Un chemin est accepté s'il remplit toutes ces conditions :
- non vide ;
- aucun `:`, ce qui couvre schéma, `host:`, `git::` et lettre de lecteur Windows. C'est plus strict que « pas de `host:` » ; un nom de fichier contenant `:` sera refusé ;
- aucun `@`, aucun `?`, aucun caractère de contrôle ;
- pas absolu, et ne commence ni par `/` ni par `\` (le chemin UNC Windows ouvrirait une connexion SMB) ;
- premier segment différent de `github.com` (casse ignorée). Sans ce point, ta règle laisserait passer `github.com/o/r` ; `./github.com/o/r` reste accepté ;
- reste dans la limite de Q1, une fois le chemin nettoyé puis les liens symboliques résolus avec `EvalSymlinks`.

Les noms avec un point (`v1.2/base`) sont acceptés. J'ai vérifié en lisant `IsRemoteFile` et `NewRepoSpecFromURL` que cette règle exclut les deux portes réseau de la version 5.8.3.

Valeurs qui ne sont pas des chemins :
- `patches[].patch`, et une entrée `patchesStrategicMerge` dont le contenu est un mapping YAML : ce sont des données, acceptées ;
- `helmCharts.repo`, `chartRepoUrl`, `helmBin`, `extraArgs` non vides : refusés comme base distante (`extraArgs` peut contenir `--repo`) ;
- une entrée de `generators`, `transformers` ou `validators` qui se lit comme un mapping : c'est une config de plugin, contrôlée comme un fichier de plugin ;
- un répertoire cité dans `generators`, `transformers` ou `validators` : on le suit en mode plugin, où ses fichiers `resources` sont lus comme des configs de plugin.

Dans une config de plugin, est refusé comme « non jugeable » tout document dont l'`apiVersion` n'est pas exactement `builtin`, dont le `kind` est inconnu, ou qui porte l'annotation `config.kubernetes.io/function` ou `config.k8s.io/function`.

**Écart entre analyseurs YAML.** kustomize lit avec `YAMLToJSON` puis le décodeur JSON, qui compare les clés en ignorant la casse, y compris le repli Unicode (`ſ` vaut `s`, `K` vaut `k`). La garde fait les mêmes correspondances avec `strings.EqualFold`, et elle échoue fermé (refus) dans tous ces cas :
- ancre ou alias, clé de fusion `<<`, tag explicite (`!!binary` cacherait une URL encodée en base64), clé qui n'est pas un scalaire ;
- clé en double (casse ignorée), clé non ASCII ;
- plusieurs documents dans une kustomization, deux fichiers kustomization dans un même répertoire ;
- clé de premier niveau inconnue ;
- valeur de référence qui n'est pas une chaîne.

Un fichier ou un répertoire de kustomization qui manque, n'est pas un fichier régulier ou est trop gros donne un refus « non jugeable ».

*Hypothèse :* une feuille absente (ex. `files: [missing.txt]`) passe et kustomize signale lui-même l'erreur. Comme elle est déjà validée lexicalement, aucun accès réseau n'est possible.

**3. Plafonds proposés** (`defaultGateLimits`, valeurs non mesurées)
- Profondeur : 16.
- Kustomizations visitées par overlay : 256, avec un mémo des répertoires déjà vus pour qu'un cycle se termine sans être signalé.
- Taille d'un fichier analysé : 4 MiB, comme `k8s.maxManifestSize`.
- Total lu par overlay : 32 MiB.
- `ctx.Err()` est vérifié à chaque fichier.

Tout dépassement donne un refus « non jugeable » qui nomme le plafond atteint.

**5. Risques et limites à documenter**
- La liste est relevée sur kustomize 5.8.3. Une version plus récente qui ajoute un champ de premier niveau voit ses overlays refusés (liste fermée). Une nouvelle façon d'aller sur le réseau à l'intérieur d'un champ déjà connu ne serait vue que par `offlineEnviron`, qui laisse passer la loopback. Je recommande une liste de champs enregistrée en `testdata` avec un test de concordance, à refaire à chaque montée de version.
- Le dépôt peut changer entre la garde et le lancement de kustomize (TOCTOU). Le dépôt est supposé immobile pendant le scan.
- Arguments ajoutés par l'utilisateur :
  - `--enable-alpha-plugins`, `--enable-exec` : ils ne servent plus à rien, puisque tout plugin non intégré est refusé ;
  - `--enable-helm` avec un chart local : `helm template` est lancé avec l'environnement coupé ; les dépendances du chart ne sont pas récupérées, ce que je n'ai pas mesuré ;
  - `--load-restrictor` : non concerné.
- Changements de comportement :
  - noms de fichier contenant `:`, `@` ou `?` refusés ;
  - champ de premier niveau inconnu refusé ;
  - références hors de la limite refusées (Q1) ;
  - le cache sert l'ancien résultat jusqu'au prochain scan ;
  - Windows n'a pas été mesuré.
- Le champ `File` du finding reste le kustomization de l'overlay (*Hypothèse*) ; le fichier qui porte la référence est nommé dans le Message.
- Coût : tous les kustomizations sont relus pour chaque overlay. Un mémo par étape de scan est possible.
- Rien d'irréversible : pas de schéma ni de clé nouvelle, un revert suffit. Pas besoin d'ADR, l'amendement de D180 suffit.

**6. Questions bloquantes :** Q1 seulement (en tête). Le titre « non jugeable » est une proposition que l'UX peut changer ; ce n'est pas bloquant.
